# Configure custom domains

A custom domain lets you reach your HCP Vault Dedicated cluster at a hostname
you own, such as `vault.example.com`, instead of the default `*.hashicorp.cloud`
address. HCP issues and renews a TLS certificate that includes your custom
domain, so clients can connect over HTTPS without certificate warnings. Your
cluster stays reachable on its default HCP address while the custom domain is
enabled.

Custom domains support publicly and privately accessible AWS and Azure clusters
in all HCP Vault Dedicated tiers. You can configure a custom domain in the HCP
Portal or with the HCP API. Your DNS records stay in your own DNS provider. The
DNS examples on this page cover AWS Route 53 and Azure DNS. If you use a
different DNS provider, create the same records in your provider.

<Note title="Public beta feature">

This feature is currently available as a _public beta release_. Beta
functionality is stable but possibly incomplete and subject to change. We
strongly discourage using beta features in production.

</Note>

## How it works

1. You create two CNAME records in the DNS zone for your domain. The first
   routes traffic for your custom domain to your cluster. The second,
   `_acme-challenge`, lets HCP prove that you control the domain so it can
   issue a certificate from Let's Encrypt.
1. You enter the custom domain in the HCP Portal, or send a `PATCH` request to
   the HCP API, to enable it on your cluster.
1. HCP checks that both CNAME records exist and point to the right place, then
   creates the certificate in the background. The setup takes 10 to 15
   minutes.

## Prerequisites

- An HCP organization and project with an existing HCP Vault Dedicated cluster,
  and permission to update that cluster. You can only configure a custom domain
  on a cluster that already exists.
- A domain you own, with a DNS zone and permission to create and delete records
  in it. For Route 53, this is a hosted zone for your primary domain. For Azure
  DNS, this is a DNS zone for your primary domain.
- (API only) The [HCP CLI](/hcp/docs/cli/install) (`hcp`), `curl`, and `jq` on
  macOS or Linux. On Windows, use WSL.
- (Optional) `dig` and `openssl`, if you want to validate CNAME propagation or
  the certificate yourself.

### Limitations

- You can configure one custom domain per cluster.
- After you enable a custom domain, you cannot update or disconnect it for 24
  hours while the configuration propagates. In the HCP Portal, the **Edit custom
  domain** and **Disconnect** buttons are visible only after this period.
- After you disconnect a custom domain, you cannot enable a custom domain on the
  same cluster for 24 hours. Refer to [Throttling](#throttling).
- HCP issues and manages the certificate. You cannot provide your own
  certificate.
- Wildcard domains, such as `*.example.com`, are not supported.

## Create the CNAME records

Both the HCP Portal and the HCP API require the same two CNAME records. Create
them in the DNS zone for your primary domain **before** you configure the custom
domain. If the records are missing or have not propagated, the configuration
fails.

Find your cluster DNS name in the **Cluster URLs** section of the cluster
overview page in the HCP Portal. Use the host name only, without `https://` and
without the port. For example,
`my-vault-cluster-public-vault-1a2b3c4d.5e6f7a8b.z1.hashicorp.cloud`.

| | Record 1: custom domain | Record 2: ACME challenge |
|---|---|---|
| **Name** | `vault` | `_acme-challenge.vault` |
| **Type** | `CNAME` | `CNAME` |
| **Value** | Your cluster DNS name | `_acme-challenge.` followed by your cluster DNS name |
| **TTL** | `300` | `300` |

For the custom domain `vault.example.com`, the records look like this:

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```text
vault.example.com                   CNAME  my-vault-cluster-public-vault-1a2b3c4d.5e6f7a8b.z1.hashicorp.cloud
_acme-challenge.vault.example.com   CNAME  _acme-challenge.my-vault-cluster-public-vault-1a2b3c4d.5e6f7a8b.z1.hashicorp.cloud
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

To create the records in AWS Route 53 or Azure DNS, refer to
[Create the records in your DNS provider](#create-the-records-in-your-dns-provider).

### Create the records in your DNS provider

Select the tab for your DNS provider.

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="AWS Route 53" group="aws">

<Note>

These steps apply only to an AWS Route 53 networking setup. If you use a
different DNS provider, create the same two records in your provider.

</Note>

1. Sign in to the AWS Management Console and open **Route 53**.

1. In the left navigation, select **Hosted zones**.

1. Select the hosted zone for your primary domain.

1. On the **Records** tab, select **Create record**.

1. Enter the values for Record 1. Set **Record type** to `CNAME`, **TTL** to
   `300`, and **Routing policy** to **Simple routing**.

1. Select **Add another record** and enter the values for Record 2.

1. Select **Create records**, then confirm both records appear on the
   **Records** tab with the values you entered.

</Tab>
<Tab heading="Azure DNS" group="azure">

<Note>

These steps apply only to an Azure DNS setup. If you use a different DNS
provider, create the same two records in your provider. For more information
about record sets in the Azure portal, refer to the
[Azure DNS documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/dns-operations-recordsets-portal).

</Note>

In Azure DNS, the record name is relative to your DNS zone. For example, in the
`example.com` zone, enter `vault` for the record `vault.example.com`.

1. Sign in to the Azure portal. In the search box at the top of the portal,
   enter **DNS zones** and select it from the results.

1. Select the DNS zone for your primary domain.

1. On the **Overview** page of the DNS zone, select **+ Record sets**, and then
   select **+ Add**.

1. On the **Add record set** page, enter the values for Record 1.

   | Setting | Value |
   |---|---|
   | **Name** | `vault` |
   | **Type** | `CNAME` |
   | **TTL** | `300` |
   | **TTL unit** | **Seconds** |
   | **Alias** | Your cluster DNS name |

   If the form shows **Alias record set**, select **No**.

1. Select **Add**.

1. Repeat steps 3 to 5 for Record 2. Set **Name** to `_acme-challenge.vault` and
   **Alias** to `_acme-challenge.` followed by your cluster DNS name.

1. On the **Recordsets** page of the DNS zone, confirm both CNAME records are
   listed with the values you entered.

</Tab>
</Tabs>

### Validate DNS propagation (optional)

DNS propagation can take a few minutes. HCP validates the records for you when
you configure the custom domain, so this check is optional. If you want to
confirm propagation first, query both records from your own network with `dig`.

```shell-session
$ dig +short CNAME vault.example.com
$ dig +short CNAME _acme-challenge.vault.example.com
```

Each command must print the matching HCP name, ending in a dot.

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```text
my-vault-cluster-public-vault-1a2b3c4d.5e6f7a8b.z1.hashicorp.cloud.
_acme-challenge.my-vault-cluster-public-vault-1a2b3c4d.5e6f7a8b.z1.hashicorp.cloud.
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

<Warning title="Wait for both records">

Do not configure the custom domain until both records resolve. If you do, the
configuration fails because HCP cannot find the CNAME records.

</Warning>

## Configure a custom domain

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="UI" group="ui">

1. Sign in to the [HCP Portal](https://portal.cloud.hashicorp.com/sign-in).

1. In the left navigation, select **Vault Dedicated**.

1. Select the cluster you want to configure from the cluster list.

1. In the cluster navigation, under **Manage**, select **Networking**.

1. In the **Communication setup** section, find the **Custom Domain** card and
   select **Connect custom domain**.

1. In the **Domain Name** field, enter your custom domain in the form
   `<subdomain>.<primary-domain>`. For example, `vault.example.com`.

1. Select **Save**.

   The portal changes the page title to **Edit custom domain**, disables
   **Save**, and shows **Validating your custom domain** with a progress
   spinner. HCP is validating your CNAME records and creating the certificate in
   the background.

1. Wait 10 to 15 minutes for the setup to complete. You can leave the page while
   HCP works. Do not try to use the custom domain until the setup completes.
   When it completes, the **Custom Domain** card on the **Networking** page
   shows **Connected**, and the **Edit custom domain** page shows **Domain
   connected successfully**.

</Tab>
<Tab heading="API" group="api">

Before you can use the HCP API, you need to sign in and generate an access
token.

### Set environment variables

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `HCP_ORGANIZATION_ID` | Your HCP organization ID. Run `hcp organizations list`. |
| `HCP_PROJECT_ID` | The ID of the project that contains your cluster. Run `hcp projects list`. |
| `HCP_VAULT_ID` | Your cluster ID, which is the cluster name. For example, `my-vault-cluster`. |
| `HCP_PROVIDER_NAME` | The cloud provider of your cluster, `aws` or `azure`. |
| `HCP_REGION_NAME` | The region of your cluster. For example, `us-west-2`. |
| `HCP_CUSTOM_DOMAIN` | The domain you want to use, in the form `<subdomain>.<primary-domain>`. For example, `vault.example.com`. |

1. Sign in to HCP.

   ```shell-session
   $ hcp auth login
   ```

1. Export the variables.

   ```shell-session
   $ export HCP_API_ADDRESS="api.cloud.hashicorp.com" \
       HCP_ORGANIZATION_ID="<HCP_ORGANIZATION_ID>" \
       HCP_PROJECT_ID="<HCP_PROJECT_ID>" \
       HCP_VAULT_ID="<HCP_VAULT_ID>" \
       HCP_PROVIDER_NAME="<aws-or-azure>" \
       HCP_REGION_NAME="<HCP_REGION_NAME>" \
       HCP_CUSTOM_DOMAIN="<subdomain>.<primary-domain>" \
       HCP_API_TOKEN="$(hcp auth print-access-token)"
   ```

   <Warning>

   The access token is a credential. Do not paste it into tickets, chat, or
   shared documents. It is short lived. If an API call returns `401`, run
   `hcp auth login` again and refresh `HCP_API_TOKEN`.

   </Warning>

### Enable the custom domain

Send a `PATCH` request to the cluster resource with `is_enabled` set to `true`.

```shell-session
$ curl --silent --show-error --request PATCH \
    "https://${HCP_API_ADDRESS}/vault/2020-11-25/organizations/${HCP_ORGANIZATION_ID}/projects/${HCP_PROJECT_ID}/clusters/${HCP_VAULT_ID}" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer ${HCP_API_TOKEN}" \
    --data @- <<EOF | jq
{
  "id": "${HCP_VAULT_ID}",
  "location": {
    "organization_id": "${HCP_ORGANIZATION_ID}",
    "project_id": "${HCP_PROJECT_ID}",
    "region": {
      "provider": "${HCP_PROVIDER_NAME}",
      "region": "${HCP_REGION_NAME}"
    }
  },
  "config": {
    "network_config": {
      "custom_domain_config": {
        "is_enabled": true,
        "custom_domain": "${HCP_CUSTOM_DOMAIN}"
      }
    }
  }
}
EOF
```

A successful request returns HTTP `200`. HCP validates your CNAME records and
creates the certificate in the background. Wait 10 to 15 minutes for the setup
to complete before you use the custom domain. If the request is rejected, refer
to [Errors](#errors).

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Verify the configuration (optional)

Verification is optional. After the 10 to 15 minute setup completes, you can
confirm that the custom domain is active.

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="UI" group="ui">

1. In the HCP Portal, open the cluster and select **Networking**.

1. In the **Custom Domain** card, confirm the status is **Connected**.

1. Select **View custom domain**. The page shows **Domain connected
   successfully** and your custom domain name.

</Tab>
<Tab heading="API" group="api">

Check the cluster configuration.

```shell-session
$ curl --silent --show-error \
    "https://${HCP_API_ADDRESS}/vault/2020-11-25/organizations/${HCP_ORGANIZATION_ID}/projects/${HCP_PROJECT_ID}/clusters/${HCP_VAULT_ID}" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer ${HCP_API_TOKEN}" | jq '.cluster.config.network_config.custom_domain_config'
```

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```json
{
  "is_enabled": true,
  "custom_domain": "vault.example.com"
}
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

</Tab>
</Tabs>

To also check the certificate and that Vault answers on your custom domain, run
the following commands from a network that can reach your cluster. A privately
accessible cluster is reachable only from networks connected to it. They require
`openssl` and `curl`.

1. Check that the certificate covers your custom domain.

   ```shell-session
   $ openssl s_client -connect vault.example.com:8200 -servername vault.example.com </dev/null 2>/dev/null \
       | openssl x509 -noout -text | grep -E "Subject:|DNS:"
   ```

   The output includes your custom domain, for example `DNS:vault.example.com`.

1. Check that Vault answers on your custom domain.

   ```shell-session
   $ curl --silent --show-error https://vault.example.com:8200/v1/sys/health
   ```

   A healthy, unsealed cluster reports `"initialized": true` and
   `"sealed": false`.

<Note>

These commands use port `8200`. If you changed the
[cluster port](/hcp/docs/vault/get-started/configure-cluster-port), use that
port instead.

</Note>

HCP renews the certificate automatically and re-validates it against your
existing CNAME records, so keep both records in place for as long as the custom
domain is enabled.

## Update a custom domain

To change the custom domain, for example from `vault.example.com` to
`vault.secrets.com`, enter the new name and save it.

<Warning title="24-hour limit">

After a custom domain connects, the HCP Portal makes changes unavailable for
24 hours while the configuration propagates. Confirm the new name before you
save it.

</Warning>

1. Create the two CNAME records for the new name in the DNS zone for its primary
   domain, as described in [Create the CNAME records](#create-the-cname-records).

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="UI" group="ui">

1. In the HCP Portal, open the cluster and select **Networking**.

1. In the **Custom Domain** card, select **Edit custom domain**.

   **Edit custom domain** is visible only 24 hours after you enable the custom
   domain. Until then, the card shows **View custom domain**, and the **Domain
   Name** field and **Save** are disabled.

1. Replace the value in the **Domain Name** field with the new name and select
   **Save**.

1. Wait 10 to 15 minutes for the setup to complete.

</Tab>
<Tab heading="API" group="api">

1. Set the new name.

   ```shell-session
   $ export HCP_CUSTOM_DOMAIN="vault.secrets.com"
   ```

1. Send the same `PATCH` request from
   [Enable the custom domain](#enable-the-custom-domain).

1. Wait 10 to 15 minutes for the setup to complete.

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Disconnect a custom domain

Disconnecting the custom domain turns it off. Your cluster stays reachable on
its default HCP address.

<Warning title="24-hour limit">

After you disconnect a custom domain, you cannot enable a custom domain on the
same cluster for 24 hours.

</Warning>

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="UI" group="ui">

1. In the HCP Portal, open the cluster and select **Networking**.

1. In the **Custom Domain** card, select **Disconnect**.

   **Disconnect** is visible only 24 hours after you enable or update the custom
   domain.

1. In the **Disconnect custom domain?** dialog, enter `DISCONNECT` in the
   **Confirm action** field, then select **Disconnect**. Select **Cancel** to
   keep the custom domain.

   The dialog confirms that the custom domain is disconnected and removed. Your
   applications continue to access Vault without interruption using the default
   domain name.

</Tab>
<Tab heading="API" group="api">

1. Send a `PATCH` request with `is_enabled` set to `false`. You do not need to
   send `custom_domain`.

   ```shell-session
   $ curl --silent --show-error --request PATCH \
       "https://${HCP_API_ADDRESS}/vault/2020-11-25/organizations/${HCP_ORGANIZATION_ID}/projects/${HCP_PROJECT_ID}/clusters/${HCP_VAULT_ID}" \
       --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
       --header "Authorization: Bearer ${HCP_API_TOKEN}" \
       --data @- <<EOF | jq
   {
     "id": "${HCP_VAULT_ID}",
     "location": {
       "organization_id": "${HCP_ORGANIZATION_ID}",
       "project_id": "${HCP_PROJECT_ID}",
       "region": {
         "provider": "${HCP_PROVIDER_NAME}",
         "region": "${HCP_REGION_NAME}"
       }
     },
     "config": {
       "network_config": {
         "custom_domain_config": {
           "is_enabled": false
         }
       }
     }
   }
   EOF
   ```

1. Wait 10 to 15 minutes for the change to complete. Your cluster remains
   reachable on its default address.

</Tab>
</Tabs>

### Clean up DNS records

After you disconnect the custom domain, or after you change to a new name and
stop using the old one, remove the two CNAME records for the name you no longer
use.

<Warning>

Do not delete the records before you disconnect or change the custom domain.
Clients that still use the custom name stop resolving as soon as the records are
gone.

</Warning>

These steps apply only to an AWS Route 53 networking setup. If you use a
different DNS provider, delete the two records in your provider.

1. In Route 53, open your hosted zone.

1. Select the check boxes next to the two records, for example
   `vault.example.com` and `_acme-challenge.vault.example.com`, then select
   **Delete records** and confirm.

## API reference

You manage custom domains through the existing HCP Vault Dedicated cluster
update endpoint. No separate endpoint exists for custom domains.

### Update cluster

`PATCH` `/vault/2020-11-25/organizations/{organization_id}/projects/{project_id}/clusters/{cluster_id}`

#### Request

The custom domain settings are in the `config.network_config.custom_domain_config`
object of the request body.

```json
{
  "id": "<cluster_id>",
  "location": {
    "organization_id": "<organization_id>",
    "project_id": "<project_id>",
    "region": {
      "provider": "<aws|azure>",
      "region": "<region>"
    }
  },
  "config": {
    "network_config": {
      "custom_domain_config": {
        "is_enabled": true,
        "custom_domain": "<subdomain>.<primary-domain>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

#### Field validation

| Field | Type | Required | Validation rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `custom_domain_config.is_enabled` | boolean | Yes | `true` enables or updates the custom domain. `false` disconnects it. |
| `custom_domain_config.custom_domain` | string | Yes when `is_enabled` is `true` | A valid fully qualified domain name (FQDN) in the form `<subdomain>.<primary-domain>`. Maximum 253 characters. Wildcards are not supported. Both CNAME records must already resolve to your cluster. |

### Errors

A rejected request returns an error body with a message and a numeric code.

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```json
{
  "error": "Failed to lookup CNAME record",
  "code": 9
}
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

| HTTP status | Error message | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `400` | `custom_domain is required when is_enabled is true` | Set `custom_domain` to a value before you send the request. |
| `400` | `Domain name too long` | Use a domain name of 253 characters or fewer. |
| `400` | `Invalid domain format` | Use the form `<subdomain>.<primary-domain>`, for example `vault.example.com`. |
| `400` | `Failed to lookup CNAME record` | A required record is missing or has not propagated. Check your [CNAME records](#create-the-cname-records), wait, and retry. |
| `400` | Empty message with code `3` | Certificate creation failed unexpectedly. Check your CNAME records and retry. If it keeps happening, contact HashiCorp support and include the time of the request. |
| `403` | `custom domain feature is not enabled` | The custom domain feature is not enabled for your organization. Contact HashiCorp support. |
| `404` | Message beginning `CNAME validation failed` | A CNAME record exists but points to the wrong target. Make sure each value matches [the records you created](#create-the-cname-records) exactly, including the `_acme-challenge.` prefix on the second record. |
| `424` | `custom domain certificate was updated recently` | You changed the custom domain within the last 24 hours, or an earlier attempt is still in its backoff period. Refer to [Throttling](#throttling). |

### Throttling

HCP creates a Let's Encrypt certificate for each custom domain change. To
protect the shared certificate issuance quota, HCP limits how often you can
change a custom domain.

- After a successful change, you cannot change the custom domain again for 24
  hours.
- If a request fails because of the throttle (HTTP `424`), HCP enforces an
  exponential backoff. The wait before you can retry grows with each failed
  attempt.

  | Retry | Wait before you can retry |
  |---|---|
  | 1st | 1 hour |
  | 2nd | 3 hours |
  | 3rd | 6 hours |
  | 4th | 12 hours |

  The ladder resets at 00:00 the next day. If a retry time falls in the next
  day's window, you can retry as early as 00:00.

## Audit logging

HCP records success and failure events for enabling, updating, and
disconnecting a custom domain in the HCP audit log. Each event includes the
cluster ID and the organization ID.

## Troubleshooting

### `Failed to lookup CNAME record` returned

Verify that:
- Both CNAME records exist in the DNS zone for your primary domain.
- Both records have propagated. `dig +short CNAME` returns the expected HCP
  name for the custom domain and for `_acme-challenge.<custom-domain>`.
- The record names match the custom domain you entered exactly.

### `CNAME validation failed` returned

Verify that:
- The value of each record matches your cluster DNS name exactly. Copy the host
  name from your cluster URL, without `https://` and without the port.
- The value of the second record starts with `_acme-challenge.`.
- The custom domain you entered is the same name you created the records for.

### `custom domain certificate was updated recently` returned

The custom domain changed within the last 24 hours, or an earlier attempt is in
its backoff period. Wait for the period described in [Throttling](#throttling)
and retry. Check the current configuration first, because the earlier request
may have already succeeded.

### The setup does not finish

The setup takes 10 to 15 minutes. If it has not finished after that, check that
both [CNAME records](#create-the-cname-records) are in place and resolve. If the
setup still does not finish, [create a support ticket](https://support.hashicorp.com/hc/en-us/requests/new)
and include the cluster ID and the time you saved the custom domain.

### The custom domain does not resolve or shows a certificate warning

- If the domain does not resolve, the first CNAME record is missing or
  incorrect. Certificate creation can succeed without it, but clients cannot
  reach the cluster until it exists.
- If the domain resolves but the browser or client shows a certificate warning,
  the `_acme-challenge` record is missing or incorrect, or the setup has not
  finished. Check the records and wait for the 10 to 15 minute setup to finish.
- For a privately accessible cluster, run your checks from a network connected
  to the cluster. Use the [connectivity tester](/hcp/docs/vault/connectivity-tester)
  to diagnose reachability from your HashiCorp Virtual Network (HVN).
